book.old: 이름이 크기를 알려 줘요. 반음은 반 걸음: 바로 옆 건반까지. 온음은 온 걸음: 반 걸음 두 개. 그리고 두 기호가 음을 반 걸음 옮겨요: 샤프는 위로, 플랫은 아래로.
book.new: 반음은 반 걸음: 바로 옆 건반까지. 온음은 온 걸음: 반 걸음 두 개. 두 기호가 음을 반 걸음 옮겨요: 샤프는 위로, 플랫은 아래로.

book.old: The names tell you the size. A semitone is a half step: to the very next key. A tone is a whole step: two half steps. And two signs move a note a half step: the sharp up, the flat down.
book.new: A semitone is a half step: to the very next key. A tone is a whole step: two half steps. Two signs move a note a half step: the sharp up, the flat down.

book.old: 피아노에서 가장 작은 걸음은 반 걸음이에요: 한 건반에서 바로 옆 건반까지, 검은건반이든 흰건반이든, 사이에 아무것도 없는 가장 가까운 이웃이에요. 이 걸음의 다른 이름은 반음이에요. 반 걸음은 오른쪽, 새가 사는 하늘 쪽으로 올라가기도 하고, 왼쪽, 거북이 사는 바다 쪽으로 내려가기도 해요.
book.new: 반 걸음은 피아노에서 가장 작은 걸음이에요: 바로 옆 건반까지, 검은건반이든 흰건반이든. 그 건반의 가장 가까운 이웃이에요. 다른 이름은 반음이에요. 위로는 오른쪽, 새가 사는 하늘 쪽. 아래로는 왼쪽, 거북이 사는 바다 쪽.

book.old: The smallest step on the piano is a half step: from a key to the very next key, black or white, with nothing in between. It is the key's nearest neighbour, the closest key there is. Its other name is a semitone (semi means half). A half step goes up to the right, towards the bird's sky, or down to the left, towards the turtle's sea.
book.new: A half step is the smallest step on the piano: to the very next key, black or white. It is the key's nearest neighbour. Its other name is a semitone (semi means half). Up is right, to the bird's sky. Down is left, to the turtle's sea.

book.old: <>반 걸음 걷기: 가운데 도에서 시작해 반 걸음씩 계속 올라가요 (검은건반, 흰건반 모두) 다음 C까지. 건반 말고 걸음을 세어요: 반 걸음 12개. 이렇게 반 걸음으로만 걷는 게 반음계(크로마틱 스케일)예요.
book.new: <>반 걸음 걷기: 가운데 도부터 다음 C까지 검은건반, 흰건반 모두 하나씩 올라가요. 건반 말고 걸음을 세어요: 반 걸음 12개. 이 걸음이 반음계(크로마틱 스케일)예요.

book.old: <>The half-step walk: start on middle C and go up a half step, again and again (every key, black and white) to the next C. Count the steps, not the keys: 12 half steps. Walking in half steps like this is the chromatic scale.
book.new: <>The half-step walk: from middle C, play every key, black and white, up to the next C. Count the steps, not the keys: 12 half steps. This walk is the chromatic scale.

book.old: 반 걸음 두 개가 온 걸음이에요: 사이에 건반 하나가 끼어 있어요. 이 걸음의 다른 이름은 온음이에요. C에서 검은건반을 넘어가면 D가 온 걸음 위예요. 검은건반끼리도 돼요: 흰건반 하나를 사이에 둔 두 검은건반도 온 걸음이에요.
book.new: 반 걸음 두 개가 온 걸음이에요: 사이에 건반 하나가 있어요. 다른 이름은 온음이에요. C에서 검은건반을 넘으면 D, 온 걸음이에요. 흰건반 하나를 사이에 둔 두 검은건반도 온 걸음이에요.

book.old: Two half steps make a whole step: one key sits in between. Its other name is a tone. From C, step over the black key: D is a whole step up. Black keys too: two black keys with one white key between them are a whole step apart.
book.new: Two half steps make a whole step: one key in between. Its other name is a tone. C to D is a whole step, over the black key. Two black keys with one white key between them are a whole step too.

book.old: <>From C, play a whole step up: step over the black key and play D. Then play a whole step up from D: E.</>
book.new: <>From C, play a whole step up: over the black key to D. Then a whole step up from D: E.</>

book.old: 흰건반을 글자 하나씩 걸어가며({bkChapterNo('note-names')}챕터의 걸음) 사이를 봐요. 대부분은 사이에 검은건반이 있어요: 온 걸음이에요. 그런데 두 군데는 없어요. 작은 집의 출구(E)로 나오면 바로 큰 집의 앞문(F)이고, 큰 집의 뒷문(B)으로 나가면 옆 작은 집의 클라라(C)가 있어요. E F와 B C는 반 걸음밖에 안 돼요.
book.new: 흰건반을 글자 하나씩 걸어요({bkChapterNo('note-names')}챕터의 걸음). 대부분은 사이에 검은건반이 있어요: 온 걸음이에요. 두 군데는 없어요. 작은 집 출구(E)로 나오면 바로 큰 집 앞문(F)이에요. 큰 집 뒷문(B)으로 나가면 옆 작은 집의 클라라(C)예요. E F와 B C는 반 걸음뿐이에요.

book.old: Walk the white keys letter by letter (Chapter {bkChapterNo('note-names')}'s steps) and look between them. Most letter steps have a black key in between: a whole step. But twice there is none. Walk out of the small house's Exit (E) and you are at the big house's Front door (F); go out of the big house's Back door (B) and there is Clara (C) at the next small house. E F and B C are only a half step apart.
book.new: Walk the white keys letter by letter (Chapter {bkChapterNo('note-names')}'s steps). Most steps have a black key in between: a whole step. Twice there is none. Out of the small house's Exit (E), you are at the big house's Front door (F). Out of the big house's Back door (B), you meet Clara (C) at the next small house. E F and B C are only a half step apart.

book.old: 샤프 {tnSign('#')}는 음을 반 걸음 위로, 오른쪽 바로 옆 건반으로 옮겨요. 플랫 {tnSign('b')}은 음을 반 걸음 아래로, 왼쪽 바로 옆 건반으로 옮겨요. 검은건반은 두 방 사이의 숨겨진 다락방 같아요. 양옆 이웃이 같이 써요. 클라라가 C에서 쓰면 C 샤프, C{tnSign('#')}, 강아지가 D에서 쓰면 D 플랫, D{tnSign('b')}이에요. 다락방 하나, 이름 둘. 그런데 E와 F 사이에는 다락방이 없어요. E에서 반 걸음 위는 바로 옆집 흰건반 F라서, E 샤프는 F와 같은 건반이에요. 샤프나 플랫이 늘 검은건반인 건 아니에요.
book.new: 샤프 {tnSign('#')}는 음을 반 걸음 위로 옮겨요. 플랫 {tnSign('b')}은 반 걸음 아래로 옮겨요. 검은건반은 양옆 이웃이 같이 쓰는 숨겨진 다락방이에요. 클라라의 C에서는 C 샤프, C{tnSign('#')}, 강아지의 D에서는 D 플랫, D{tnSign('b')}이에요. 다락방 하나, 이름 둘. E와 F 사이에는 다락방이 없어서, E 샤프는 흰건반 F예요. 샤프나 플랫이 늘 검은건반은 아니에요.

book.old: The sharp sign {tnSign('#')} moves a note up a half step, to the very next key on the right. The flat sign {tnSign('b')} moves a note down a half step, to the very next key on the left. A black key is like a hidden attic between two rooms, shared by the neighbours on each side. When Clara uses it from C, it is C sharp, C{tnSign('#')}. When the Dog uses it from D, it is D flat, D{tnSign('b')}. One attic, two names. But between E and F there is no attic: a half step up from E is the white key F next door, so E sharp is the same key as F. A sharp or a flat is not always a black key.
book.new: The sharp sign {tnSign('#')} moves a note up a half step. The flat sign {tnSign('b')} moves it down a half step. A black key is a hidden attic shared by the neighbours on each side. From Clara's C, it is C sharp, C{tnSign('#')}. From the Dog's D, it is D flat, D{tnSign('b')}. One attic, two names. Between E and F there is no attic, so E sharp is the white key F. A sharp or a flat is not always a black key.

book.old: 오선에서는 기호를 음표 바로 앞, 음표 머리와 같은 줄이나 칸에 써요: 샤프의 작은 상자와 플랫의 동그란 배가 바로 그 줄이나 칸에 앉아요. 읽을 때는 글자 먼저, 기호는 나중에: "F 샤프", "B 플랫". 쓰는 순서는 반대예요: 기호 먼저, 음표는 그 뒤에.
book.new: 오선에서는 기호를 음표 바로 앞, 음표 머리와 같은 줄이나 칸에 써요. 샤프의 작은 상자와 플랫의 동그란 배가 그 줄이나 칸에 앉아요. 읽을 때는 글자 먼저: "F 샤프", "B 플랫". 쓸 때는 기호 먼저.

book.old: On the staff, the sign goes just before the note, on the same line or space as its head: the sharp's little box and the flat's round belly sit right on that line or space. Say the letter first, then the sign: "F sharp", "B flat". Write them the other way round: the sign first, then the note.
book.new: On the staff, the sign goes just before the note, on the same line or space as its head. The sharp's little box and the flat's round belly sit on it. Say the letter first: "F sharp", "B flat". Write the sign first.

guide.old: The names tell you the size. A semitone is a half step, to the very next key. A tone is a whole step: two half steps. And two signs move a note by a half step: the sharp up, the flat down.
guide.new: A semitone is a half step, to the very next key. A tone is a whole step: two half steps. Two signs move a note by a half step: the sharp up, the flat down.

guide.old: The smallest step on the piano is a half step: from a key to the very next key, black or white, with nothing in between. It is the key's nearest neighbour.
guide.new: A half step is the smallest step on the piano: to the very next key, black or white. It is the key's nearest neighbour.

guide.old: From D, a half step up and a half step down both land on black keys. From a black key, both land on white keys.
guide.new: From D, both half steps land on black keys. From a black key, both land on white keys.

guide.old: Start on C and go up a half step, again and again, every key, black and white, to the next C: that is 12 half steps. Walking in half steps like this is the chromatic scale.
guide.new: From C, play every key, black and white, up to the next C: 12 half steps. This walk is the chromatic scale.

guide.old: Two half steps make a whole step, with one key in between. Its other name is a tone. From C, step over the black key: D is a whole step up. Black keys too: two black keys with one white key between them are a whole step apart.
guide.new: Two half steps make a whole step, with one key in between. Its other name is a tone. C to D is a whole step, over the black key. Two black keys with one white key between them are a whole step too.

guide.old: Walk up the white keys letter by letter and look between them. Most letter steps have a black key in between, so they are whole steps. But twice there is none.
guide.new: Walk up the white keys letter by letter. Most steps have a black key in between: whole steps. Twice there is none.

guide.old: From the last key of the small house (E) to the first key of the big house (F), and from the last key of the big house (B) to C at the next small house, there is no black key. E F and B C are only a half step apart.
guide.new: E ends the small house and F starts the big house. B ends the big house and C starts the next small house. E F and B C are only a half step apart.

guide.old: Walk the white keys from C up to the next C, naming each step, and you get whole, whole, half, whole, whole, whole, half. That order is the recipe for the major scale, which the Scales chapter builds with it.
guide.new: From C up to the next C, the white keys go whole, whole, half, whole, whole, whole, half. That order is the major scale's recipe. The Scales chapter builds scales with it.

guide.old: The sharp sign ♯ moves a note up a half step, to the very next key on the right. The flat sign ♭ moves a note down a half step, to the very next key on the left.
guide.new: The sharp sign ♯ moves a note up a half step. The flat sign ♭ moves it down a half step.

guide.old: A black key is like a hidden attic between two rooms, shared by the neighbours on each side. When Clara uses it from C, it is C sharp, C♯. When the Dog uses it from D, it is D flat, D♭. One attic, two names.
guide.new: A black key is a hidden attic shared by the neighbours on each side. From Clara's C, it is C sharp, C♯. From the Dog's D, it is D flat, D♭. One attic, two names.

guide.old: But between E and F there is no attic. A half step up from E is the white key F next door, so E sharp is the same key as F. A sharp or a flat is not always a black key.
guide.new: Between E and F there is no attic, so E sharp is the white key F. A sharp or a flat is not always a black key.

guide.old: On the staff, the sign goes just before the note, on the same line or space as its head: the sharp's little box and the flat's round belly sit right on that line or space.
guide.new: On the staff, the sign goes just before the note, on the same line or space as its head. The sharp's little box and the flat's round belly sit on it.

guide.old: Say the letter first, then the sign: "F sharp", "B flat". Write them the other way round: the sign first, then the note.
guide.new: Say the letter first: "F sharp", "B flat". Write the sign first.

guide.old: A semitone is the smallest step on the piano: from one key to the very next key, black or white, with nothing in between. Its other name is a half step. Twelve semitones take you from one C to the next C.
guide.new: A semitone is the smallest step on the piano: to the very next key, black or white. Its other name is a half step. Twelve semitones take you from one C to the next.

guide.old: A tone (a whole step) is two semitones (two half steps): there is one key in between. From C to D is a tone, because the black key C sharp sits between them. From E to F is a semitone, because there is no key between them.
guide.new: A tone (a whole step) is two semitones (two half steps), with one key in between. C to D is a tone: the black key C sharp sits between them. E to F is a semitone: no key sits between them.

guide.old: Because there is no black key between them. Every other pair of white neighbours has a black key in between, so it is a tone. That is why the white keys from C to C go whole, whole, half, whole, whole, whole, half.
guide.new: Because there is no black key between them. Every other pair of white neighbours has one, so it is a tone. That is why the white keys from C to C go whole, whole, half, whole, whole, whole, half.

guide.old: A black key can be reached from either side. A half step up from C, it is C sharp; a half step down from D, it is D flat. It is the same key, like an attic shared by the neighbours on each side.
guide.new: A black key can be reached from either side. A half step up from C, it is C sharp. A half step down from D, it is D flat. One key, like an attic shared by the neighbours on each side.

guide.old: No. A sharp is the very next key up, black or white. A half step up from E is the white key F, so E sharp is the same key as F; in the same way, C flat is the same key as B. Beginners mostly meet sharps and flats on the black keys, and these white-key names come later, with scales.
guide.new: No. A sharp is the very next key up, black or white. So E sharp is the white key F, and C flat is B. Beginners meet sharps and flats mostly on black keys. The white-key names come later, with scales.
